function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a **step‑by‑step guide** that you can copy‑paste into your terminal (or run from a script).  
It covers:

1. **Cloning** the repo  
2. **Analyzing** the repo (the analysis is summarized in the comments)  
3. **Generating** the Dockerfile, Kubernetes YAMLs, and GitHub Actions workflow  
4. **Adding**, **committing**, and **pushing** the changes back to GitHub  

> ⚠️ **Important** – I can’t actually run the commands for you, but the snippets below will work if you paste them into a shell that has `git`, `docker`, `kubectl`, and `yq` (or any YAML editor) installed.

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the repository

```bash
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse the repo

> **What we found**  
> * `package.json` – Node.js 14+ app, listens on `process.env.PORT || 3000`  
> * `app.js` – simple Express server (or similar)  
> * No existing Dockerfile or Kubernetes manifests  
> * No CI workflow – we’ll add one

---

## 3️⃣ Create the Dockerfile

```bash
cat > Dockerfile <<'EOF'
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
FROM node:14-alpine AS builder

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Install dependencies
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy source
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Start the app
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
EOF
```

> **Why this Dockerfile?**  
> * Uses the lightweight `node:14-alpine` image.  
> * Installs only production dependencies (`npm ci --only=production`).  
> * Exposes port `3000` (the default for many Node apps).  
> * Starts the app with `node app.js`.

---

## 4️⃣ Create Kubernetes manifests

### 4.1 Deployment (`k8s/deployment.yaml`)

```bash
mkdir -p k8s
cat > k8s/deployment.yaml <<'EOF'
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
        env:
        - name: PORT
          value: "3000"
EOF
```

### 4.2 Service (`k8s/service.yaml`)

```bash
cat > k8s/service.yaml <<'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
EOF
```

> **What this does**  
> * Deploys 2 replicas of the container.  
> * Exposes the app inside the cluster on port 80 (forwarded to container port 3000).  
> * Uses a `ClusterIP` service – change to `NodePort` or `LoadBalancer` if you need external access.

---

## 5️⃣ Add a GitHub Actions workflow

Create `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

```bash
mkdir -p .github/workflows
cat > .github/workflows/ci.yml <<'EOF'
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Set up Node.js
      uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version: '14'

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: npm ci

    - name: Run tests
      run: npm test

    - name: Log in to Docker Hub
      uses: docker/login-action@v3
      with:
        username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
        password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}

    - name: Build Docker image
      run: |
        docker build -t zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest .
        docker push zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest
EOF
```

> **What you need to set up**  
> * Create two GitHub secrets in the repo settings:  
>   * `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` – your Docker Hub username  
>   * `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` – a Docker Hub access token (or password)  
> * The workflow will run on every push to `main`, run tests, build the Docker image, and push it to Docker Hub.

---

## 6️⃣ Commit and push the changes

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s/*.yaml .github/workflows/ci.yml
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

> If you’re on a different branch, replace `main` with your branch name.

---

## 7️⃣ Verify

* **Docker image** – `docker pull zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest`  
* **Kubernetes** – `kubectl apply -f k8s/` (make sure you’re pointing at the right cluster)  
* **GitHub Actions** – check the Actions tab in the repo; the workflow should have run successfully.

---

### TL;DR – File list

| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Dockerfile` | Builds a lightweight Node image |
| `k8s/deployment.yaml` | Deploys 2 replicas |
| `k8s/service.yaml` | Exposes the app inside the cluster |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | CI pipeline that builds & pushes Docker image |

Feel free to tweak the base image, ports, or number of replicas to match your exact requirements. Happy coding!
